incidents.victim: North American academic, medical and military research institutions
incidents.vector: A China-nexus group ran a stealthy cross-sector intrusion campaign that quietly harvested research data and went undetected for more than a year.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group disclosed a sophisticated campaign against the North American academic, medical and military research community, with long-term undetected access enabling theft of sensitive research.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a zero-day privilege-escalation flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager to escalate from a compromised admin account to root-level control of network infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Mandiant reported active exploitation that gave attackers the highest level of access at a communications provider; researchers say the flaw was being hit as much as two months before public disclosure.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a critical authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-48558) in SimpleHelp remote management software to gain technician-level access, then deployed a JavaScript loader (TaskWeaver) and the Djinn Stealer payload.
incidents.impact: Djinn Stealer strips developer and admin machines of cloud credentials, SSH/API keys, package-registry logins (npm, PyPI, NuGet) and AI-tool config files for Claude, Gemini and Codex, enabling downstream supply-chain compromise.

incidents.vector: A long-running operation published 119+ malicious Edge, Chrome and Firefox extensions through 90+ developer accounts, using steganography to hide payloads that activated three-to-five days after install.
incidents.impact: Microsoft took down the 'StegoAd' extensions, which stole credentials, backdoored browsers and ran ad/search-affiliate fraud; more than 2.6 million users are believed to have installed them.

incidents.victim: Chromium browser users seeking AI search tools
incidents.vector: A malicious Chromium extension spoofed Perplexity AI using a typosquatted domain and abused Manifest V3 declarativeNetRequest rules to intercept every Omnibox query and keystroke before redirecting to real search engines.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Threat Intelligence found the extension exfiltrated full search queries and keystroke-level input to attacker infrastructure for profiling; Google removed it after disclosure.

incidents.victim: Government officials, journalists and military personnel (US, Europe, Ukraine)
incidents.attacker: Russia — FSB intelligence service and military intelligence
incidents.vector: Russian intelligence operators impersonated Signal and WhatsApp support accounts and altered group-invite pages to phish verification codes, account PINs and backup recovery keys from high-value targets.
incidents.impact: FBI and CISA updated their public advisory as the campaign evolved to steal backup recovery keys that survive account resets; the State Department posted a $10 million reward for information on the two responsible groups.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the public email service operated by Japanese telecom KDDI and shared by five other ISPs.
incidents.impact: Attackers made off with the data of more than 14 million users of the email service.

incidents.vector: Japan's military used USB drives infected with Chinese malware that were connected to classified networks.
incidents.impact: The breach went undisclosed for nearly a year before being uncovered by reporters; it is unclear what classified data was stolen, and Japan is now notifying NATO partners of a possible leak.

incidents.victim: John Bolton (former US National Security Advisor)
incidents.vector: A cyber actor believed linked to Iran hacked Bolton's personal email account after he left office, an account he had used to send classified 'diary' notes to unauthorized family members.
incidents.impact: Disclosed via Bolton's guilty plea to retaining national defense information; prosecutors said the hack exposed top-secret material, including foreign military plans and covert US operations, to an adversary.

incidents.vector: A coordinated Europol operation with seven law-enforcement agencies and six security firms seized infrastructure behind the Amadey loader and StealC infostealer.
incidents.impact: Authorities took down 326 servers, 142 domains and over $47M in crypto profits; the operations had infected 140,000+ computers and stolen 27 million-plus credentials over their lifetime.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached one of Polymarket's third-party vendors and loaded malicious code onto the prediction-market website.
incidents.impact: Roughly $3 million was stolen from users before the compromise was detected; Polymarket pledged to reimburse affected customers.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack disrupted operations at one of India's largest automakers, impacting an engineering and research subsidiary.
incidents.impact: Bajaj Auto disclosed the incident to market authorities; the attack affected a subsidiary supporting its two- and three-wheel vehicle business.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack knocked out Ukrposhta's mobile app and several web services.
incidents.impact: Ukraine's national postal operator was forced to work to restore customer-facing digital services after the disruption.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian government and state-owned energy entities
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking actors (tracked as CL-STA-1062) exploited web applications to drop ASPX web shells, then used SoftEther VPN, Mimikatz and a new bespoke backdoor (TinyRCT) for persistence and data theft.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 detailed compromises of a Southeast Asian government entity and at least two state-owned critical energy infrastructure operators, with full-lifecycle intrusions covering reconnaissance through database and source-code exfiltration.

incidents.vector: The World Leaks extortion group listed Tata Electronics as a victim and claimed theft of more than 200,000 documents.
incidents.impact: Tata Electronics confirmed a breach; the stolen files allegedly contain sensitive data on Apple and Tesla electronic components.

incidents.victim: Education-sector and public organizations (incl. University of Nottingham, Council of Europe)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters (UNC6240) ran an active compromise-and-extortion campaign exploiting Oracle PeopleSoft application infrastructure, alongside other intrusions claimed on its leak site.
incidents.impact: Mandiant and GTIG flagged the PeopleSoft campaign against the education sector; ShinyHunters separately claimed theft from the University of Nottingham and listed 297GB allegedly stolen from the Council of Europe.

incidents.victim: Transport for London, M&S, Co-op, US healthcare providers (Scattered Spider cases)
incidents.vector: Scattered Spider members used SIM-swapping and SMS/voice phishing to steal credentials and breach corporate networks, including the August 2024 attack that crippled Transport for London.
incidents.impact: Two key members pleaded guilty in the UK on day one of their trial; related indictments tie the group to 120 intrusions at 47 US entities and at least $115M in ransom payments.

incidents.vector: Attackers stole data from a company that managed the agency's mobile device management platform, in activity linked to a wave of attacks on Ivanti EPMM servers last year.
incidents.impact: The names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian intelligence service employees were exposed.

incidents.victim: Klue customers (security firms incl. Huntress, Snyk, Recorded Future, LastPass)
incidents.vector: Attackers used a compromised legacy credential to breach business-intelligence platform Klue, stole customers' OAuth tokens, then used them to log into connected Salesforce accounts and download data.
incidents.impact: Roughly 20 companies have confirmed breaches; a group calling itself 'Icarus' (with ShinyHunters hallmarks) is extorting Klue and victims to prevent data leaks.

incidents.victim: 18,000+ online stores using the Okendo Reviews widget
incidents.vector: A threat actor (tracked as SmartApeSG) compromised the widely embedded Okendo Reviews widget and injected JavaScript that ran a ClickFix lure, tricking shoppers into pasting malicious commands into their terminal.
incidents.impact: The supply-chain compromise exposed customers of more than 18,000 online stores to infostealer and RAT delivery before the widget was restored to a safe version.

incidents.vector: A hacker breached Brazil's national emergency alert system and pushed a false extreme-level alert to mobile phones across five regions.
incidents.impact: Residents of major cities including Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Brasilia received a spoofed alarm reading 'misantropy'; the government took the alert system offline in response.

incidents.victim: 73,932 FortiGate firewalls / VPN gateways worldwide (govt, CNI, multinationals)
incidents.vector: A Russian-speaking actor ('SantaAd') ran a months-long mass-scanning and brute-force campaign against Fortinet, Sophos, Citrix and MSSQL, deployed a custom 'FortigateSniffer' to intercept credentials in transit, and cracked harvested hashes on a 45-GPU cluster.
incidents.impact: The 'FortiBleed' dataset exposed valid admin and SSL-VPN credentials for ~73,932 FortiGate devices across 194 countries; confirmed victims include a Turkish NATO defense contractor from which classified documents were allegedly exfiltrated, and access is being sold to other groups.
